title: Select all columns from employees
body: Return every column from the `employees` table.
solution:
SELECT *
FROM employees;

title: Select specific columns
body: Return `name` and `salary` from `employees`.
solution:
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees;

title: Filter by salary
body: Employees with salary greater than 5000.

title: Filter by department
body: Employees in the IT department.

title: AND condition
body: IT employees earning more than 6000.
solution:
SELECT *
FROM employees
WHERE department = 'IT'
  AND salary > 6000;

title: OR condition
body: Employees in IT or HR.

title: BETWEEN
body: Salaries between 5000 and 8000 inclusive.

title: IN operator
body: Departments IT, HR, or Finance.

title: LIKE starts with
body: Names starting with 'A'.

title: LIKE contains
body: Names containing 'an' (case depends on collation).

title: IS NULL
body: Employees with no manager.

title: IS NOT NULL
body: Employees who have a manager.

title: ORDER BY ascending
body: Employees sorted by salary ascending.

title: ORDER BY descending
body: Top salaries first.

title: TOP N rows
body: Top 5 highest-paid employees (SQL Server).

title: Column alias
body: Show name and salary as `employee_salary`.
solution:
SELECT name, salary AS employee_salary
FROM employees;

title: DISTINCT departments
body: List unique departments.
solution:
SELECT DISTINCT department
FROM employees;

title: COUNT all rows
body: Total number of employees.
solution:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_employees
FROM employees;

title: COUNT non-null
body: Count employees with a phone number.
solution:
SELECT COUNT(phone) AS employees_with_phone
FROM employees;

title: SUM salary
body: Total payroll.
solution:
SELECT SUM(salary) AS total_payroll
FROM employees;

title: AVG salary
body: Average salary.
solution:
SELECT AVG(salary) AS avg_salary
FROM employees;

title: MIN and MAX salary
body: Lowest and highest salary.
solution:
SELECT MIN(salary) AS min_sal, MAX(salary) AS max_sal
FROM employees;

title: GROUP BY department
body: Employee count per department.

title: GROUP BY with AVG
body: Average salary per department.

title: HAVING filter
body: Departments with more than 5 employees.
solution:
SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM employees
GROUP BY department
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

title: WHERE + GROUP BY + HAVING
body: Departments where avg salary > 7000 (only include salaries >= 5000 in rows before group).
solution:
SELECT department, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary
FROM employees
WHERE salary >= 5000
GROUP BY department
HAVING AVG(salary) > 7000;

title: CASE salary band
body: Label salaries High/Medium/Low.
solution:
SELECT name, salary,
  CASE
    WHEN salary >= 8000 THEN 'High'
    WHEN salary >= 5000 THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Low'
  END AS band
FROM employees;

title: COALESCE phone
body: Show phone or 'Not Available'.
solution:
SELECT name, COALESCE(phone, 'Not Available') AS phone
FROM employees;

title: Arithmetic column
body: Annual salary (salary * 12).
solution:
SELECT name, salary, salary * 12 AS annual_salary
FROM employees;

title: INNER JOIN
body:
Employee names with department names.

`employees(emp_id, name, dept_id)` + `departments(dept_id, dept_name)`

title: LEFT JOIN
body: All employees and dept name (NULL if missing).

title: Filter joined table
body:
Orders with customer name where amount > 1000.

`orders(order_id, customer_id, amount)` + `customers(customer_id, name)`
solution:
SELECT o.order_id, c.name, o.amount
FROM orders o
INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.amount > 1000;

title: Multiple JOINs
body: Order id, customer name, product name.
solution:
SELECT o.order_id, c.name AS customer, p.product_name
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id;

title: GROUP BY after JOIN
body: Total order amount per customer.
solution:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name;

title: COUNT orders per customer
body: How many orders each customer placed.

title: DELETE syntax (concept)
body: Delete employees in a closed department named 'Temp'. **Do not run on prod.**
solution:
DELETE FROM employees
WHERE department = 'Temp';

title: UPDATE syntax (concept)
body: Give 10% raise to IT department.

title: INSERT single row
body: Insert one employee row.
solution:
INSERT INTO employees (emp_id, name, department, salary)
VALUES (101, 'Rahul', 'IT', 6000);

title: INSERT multiple rows
body: Insert two employees in one statement.
solution:
INSERT INTO employees (emp_id, name, department, salary)
VALUES
  (102, 'Amit', 'HR', 5000),
  (103, 'Priya', 'IT', 8000);

title: Subquery scalar
body: Employees earning above company average.

title: Subquery IN
body: Employees in departments with avg salary > 7000.
solution:
SELECT *
FROM employees
WHERE department IN (
  SELECT department
  FROM employees
  GROUP BY department
  HAVING AVG(salary) > 7000
);

title: NOT EXISTS

body: All cities from customers and suppliers (deduped).

title: Simple CTE

title: Percentage of total
body: Each department's share of total salary (basic subquery).
solution:
SELECT department,
  SUM(salary) AS dept_total,
  SUM(salary) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(salary) FROM employees) AS pct
FROM employees
GROUP BY department;

title: Filter NULL with COALESCE in ORDER
body: Sort by salary treating NULL as 0.

title: Self join preview
body: Employee name with manager name (`manager_id` → `emp_id`).

title: Date filter range
body: Orders in year 2024 without applying function on column.
solution:
SELECT *
FROM orders
WHERE order_date >= '2024-01-01'
  AND order_date < '2025-01-01';

title: Correlated subquery
body: Employees earning more than their department average.
solution:
SELECT e.*
FROM employees e
WHERE e.salary > (
  SELECT AVG(e2.salary)
  FROM employees e2
  WHERE e2.department = e.department
);

body: Departments with total salary > 50000.

title: Multiple CTEs
body: High earners in high-budget departments.

body: Rank all employees by salary.

body: Rank salaries allowing ties with gaps.

title: DENSE_RANK
body: Rank salaries without gaps after ties.

title: Top 3 per department
body: Top 3 earners in each department.

title: LAG previous salary
body: Show salary and previous month's salary from `salary_history(emp_id, salary, effective_date)`.

title: LEAD next order
body: Next order date per customer from `orders(customer_id, order_date)`.

body: Cumulative revenue by date from `sales(sale_date, revenue)`.

title: Running total per customer
body: Running order amount per customer.

title: Moving average 3-day
body: 3-row moving average of revenue.

title: Dept avg with window
body: Each employee vs department average without GROUP BY collapse.

body: Split employees into 4 salary buckets.

body: Highest salary in each department shown on every row.

title: Find duplicates by email
body: Emails appearing more than once in `customers(email)`.
solution:
SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM customers

HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

title: Latest record per key
body: Latest row per `customer_id` from `customer_history(customer_id, updated_at, ...)`.

body: Using window instead of correlated subquery.

title: EXCEPT non-ordering customers
body: Customers who never ordered.

title: SELF JOIN managers
body: Employees earning more than their manager.
solution:
SELECT e.name AS employee, e.salary AS emp_sal, m.name AS manager, m.salary AS mgr_sal
FROM employees e
JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id
WHERE e.salary > m.salary;

title: Managers with 5+ reports
body: Managers with at least 5 direct reports.
solution:
SELECT manager_id, COUNT(*) AS report_count
FROM employees
WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY manager_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;

title: CROSS JOIN count
body: How many rows from CROSS JOIN of 3 employees × 4 departments? **Write query to verify.**

body: All employees and departments even without match.

body: All departments and matching employees.

title: Pivot with CASE
body: Sales per product as columns from `sales(product, amount)`.
solution:
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN product = 'A' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS product_a,
  SUM(CASE WHEN product = 'B' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS product_b
FROM sales;

title: Month-over-month change
body: Revenue change vs previous month from `monthly_revenue(month, revenue)`.
solution:
WITH x AS (
  SELECT month, revenue,
    LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev
  FROM monthly_revenue
)
SELECT month, revenue, revenue - prev AS change
FROM x;

title: MoM growth %
body: Month-over-month growth percentage.
solution:
WITH x AS (
  SELECT month, revenue,
    LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev
  FROM monthly_revenue
)
SELECT month,
  (revenue - prev) * 100.0 / NULLIF(prev, 0) AS growth_pct
FROM x;

title: Salary increase detection
body: Rows where salary increased vs previous effective date.

title: Products never sold
body: Products with no rows in `order_items`.

title: Customers spending > 100k

solution:
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(amount) > 100000;

title: Customers with 3+ orders
body: Customers with more than 3 orders.
solution:
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;

title: Highest order per customer
body: The order row with max amount per customer.

title: Department max headcount

title: Percentage contribution
body: Each department's % of total salary using window.
solution:
SELECT department, SUM(salary) AS dept_sal,
  SUM(salary) * 100.0 / SUM(SUM(salary)) OVER () AS pct
FROM employees
GROUP BY department;

title: Recursive CTE hierarchy
body: Employee hierarchy levels from CEO (`manager_id IS NULL`).
solution:
WITH RECURSIVE eh AS (
  SELECT emp_id, name, manager_id, 0 AS lvl
  FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.emp_id, e.name, e.manager_id, eh.lvl + 1
  FROM employees e
  JOIN eh ON e.manager_id = eh.emp_id
)
SELECT * FROM eh;

solution:
SELECT c.*, o.order_id
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o.status = 'ACTIVE';

title: Conditional aggregate
body: Count active vs inactive employees in one query (`status` column).
solution:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'ACTIVE') AS active_cnt,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'INACTIVE') AS inactive_cnt
FROM employees;

title: SQL Server conditional count
body: Same using SUM(CASE) for SQL Server.
solution:
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'ACTIVE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_cnt,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'INACTIVE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inactive_cnt
FROM employees;

FROM calendar c
LEFT JOIN sales s ON c.dt = s.sale_date
WHERE s.sale_date IS NULL;

title: Gaps in dates
body: Missing dates between min and max in `sales(sale_date)` — use calendar join.
solution:
SELECT c.dt AS missing_date
FROM calendar c
WHERE c.dt BETWEEN (SELECT MIN(sale_date) FROM sales)
                   AND (SELECT MAX(sale_date) FROM sales)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales s WHERE s.sale_date = c.dt);

title: YoY comparison
body: Compare revenue same month year-over-year.
solution:
SELECT month, revenue,
  LAG(revenue, 12) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS revenue_prev_year,
  revenue - LAG(revenue, 12) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS yoy_change

title: Cumulative distinct customers

title: SCD Type 2 expire
body: Expire current dimension row when city changes (conceptual MERGE step 1).
solution:
UPDATE dim_customer
SET end_date = CAST(GETDATE() AS date), is_current = 0
FROM dim_customer t
JOIN staging_customer s ON t.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE t.is_current = 1 AND t.city <> s.city;

title: SCD Type 2 insert
body: Insert new version after expire (conceptual step 2).
solution:
INSERT INTO dim_customer (customer_id, city, start_date, end_date, is_current)
SELECT s.customer_id, s.city, CAST(GETDATE() AS date), '9999-12-31', 1
FROM staging_customer s
JOIN dim_customer t ON s.customer_id = t.customer_id AND t.is_current = 1
WHERE t.city <> s.city;

body: Current rows from SCD2 `dim(cust_id, city, start_dt, end_dt, is_current)`.
solution: SELECT * FROM dim_customer WHERE is_current = 1;

solution:

body: Amount of each customer's first order.

SELECT *

WHERE hire_date < '2025-04-01'

title: Churn definition
body: Customers whose last order was > 90 days ago.
solution:
SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_date) AS last_order
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING MAX(order_date) < DATEADD(day, -90, CAST(GETDATE() AS date));

title: Revenue per employee
body: Company revenue divided by employee count (scalar subqueries).

title: Bucket salaries
body: Assign custom salary buckets 0-5k, 5-8k, 8k+.
solution:
SELECT name, salary,
  CASE
    WHEN salary < 5000 THEN '0-5k'
    WHEN salary < 8000 THEN '5-8k'

title: Merge upsert pattern
body: Conceptual MERGE for `target` from `source` on `id`.
solution:
MERGE target AS t
USING source AS s ON t.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.val = s.val
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, val) VALUES (s.id, s.val);

title: Late arriving fact
body: Attach fact to current dimension version by business key.
solution:
SELECT f.*, d.surrogate_key
FROM fact_sales f
JOIN dim_product d
  ON f.product_bk = d.product_bk AND d.is_current = 1;

title: Histogram buckets
body: Count employees per 2000 salary bucket.
solution:
SELECT (salary / 2000) * 2000 AS bucket_start, COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM employees
GROUP BY (salary / 2000) * 2000
ORDER BY bucket_start;
